E. System Architecture

ms.promise:
A. Matching Engine Alpha
 An alpha matching engine implementing price–time priority, partial fills, cancels, IOC and limit orders, with deterministic replay.
B. Data Path Implementation
 A data ingestion path including a synthetic map runner and optional delayed feed adapter, with pluggable schemas supporting multiple asset classes.
C. Custom Market Configuration Support
 Configurable market definitions using YAML or JSON, covering trading hours, tick size, lot size, halts, and holidays.
D. Anchoring Service Alpha
 A service that periodically commits matching engine state hashes on-chain and exposes a verification endpoint.
E. UI and SDK Alpha
 A minimal React-based UI and alpha SDKs (Python and TypeScript) supporting order submission, market views, and basic metrics.
F. Testing and CI Environment
 A reproducible testing environment including containers, seeded scenarios, local scripts, and continuous integration test suites.
ms.criteria:

C1. Custom Market Configuration Support
 At least 2 market configurations load correctly from YAML or JSON and are applied at runtime.
D1. Anchoring Service Alpha
 At least 1 successful on-chain state hash commit is produced and verified using the service’s veri
ms.report:
A. Output: Matching engine alpha: price–time priority, partial fills, cancels, IOC and limit orders, with deterministic replay (@hydra-ws/core).
Acceptance criteria (A1): At least one end-to-end trading scenario runs order placement, partial fill, cancel, and deterministic replay without critical crashes.
Evidence (A2):
・Implementation: packages/core/src/engine.ts, packages/core/src/eventLog.ts, packages/core/src/replay.ts
・Scenario: examples/scenario-trade.mjs
・Reproducible capture script (development docs): docs/development/scripts/capture-scenario-trade.sh
・CI exercises the scenario on a clean runner: .github/workflows/ci.yml (job ts, step scenario-trade.mjs)
・Successful workflow runs: GitHub Actions — CI workflow

B. Output: Data path with synthetic feed and an external adapter path (e.g. Alpaca market data) producing normalized events.
Acceptance criteria (B1): At least two data sources (synthetic runner and one adapter) load and produce normalized events using defined schemas.

・Synthetic: packages/core/src/synthetic.ts
・Adapter + normalization: packages/adapters-alpaca/src/marketData.ts, packages/adapters-alpaca/src/index.ts
・Example usage: examples/btc-paper-hft-sim.mjs, examples/alpaca-account.mjs
・Development capture: docs/development/scripts/capture-data-path.mjs, docs/development/scripts/capture-data-path.sh

C. Output: Custom market configuration (YAML/JSON) for tick size, lot size, hours, halts, holidays, applied at runtime.
Acceptance criteria (C1): At least two market configurations load from YAML or JSON and apply at runtime.
Evidence (C2):
・Config files: markets/aapl.yaml, markets/btcusdt.json (and markets/us_equity.yaml)
・Loader and runtime application: packages/market-config/src/loader.ts, packages/market-config/src/apply.ts
・Capture script: docs/development/scripts/capture-market-config.mjs

D. Output: Anchoring service alpha: periodic state-hash commits (mock or Hydra-backed transport) and a verification endpoint.
